contributions.headingText: Clear cell adenocarcinoma is an adenocarcinoma with cellular atypia; clear and eosinophilic cytoplasm; and tubulocystic, papillary, and solid growth patterns. It is thought to be of Müllerian origin.
2C9Y & XH6L02 Other specified malignant neoplasms of urinary tract & Clear cell adenocarcinoma, NOS

Acceptable: Müllerian-type tumour, clear cell type.

Not recommended: mesonephric carcinoma; mesonephroma.

Clear cell adenocarcinomas are mostly seen in the urethra, but they also occur in the bladder. They are frequently associated with Müllerianosis. Rare cases invading the prostate, periprostatic tissue, or renal pelvis have been described {32960833; 31555949; 31947882}. Clear cell adenocarcinomas may originate from a Müllerian duct cyst {7282633} or a urethral diverticulum in the female and male (periprostatic) embryological remnants or prostatic utricle {12837455; 30089340; 32960833}.

The tumour shows a female predominance (M:F ratio: 1:4.6), with patient age ranging from 8 to 93 years. Patients typically present with haematuria or urinary symptoms. Frequently, the tumour is at an advanced stage at diagnosis, with nodal and distant metastases {31947882}.
This is a relatively rare tumour, with about 250 cases reported in the English-language literature {32960833}.

The histogenesis of clear cell adenocarcinoma is debated; hypotheses include origins from the urothelium, pre-existing Müllerian precursors, or mesonephric remnants (Wolffian ducts). Urothelial origin is supported by the occasional presence of a neoplastic urothelial component {23307189; 14634422; 18788852} and similar chromosomal abnormalities to those observed in urothelial carcinoma using UroVysion FISH and X-chromosome inactivation pattern analysis {18381932}. A Müllerian origin is supported by the female predominance, similarities with tumours arising in the female genital tract {31372739; 11444201}, and occasional association with endometriosis (including malignant transformation of endometriosis of the bladder) {2707751; 22754140}. Rarely, there is an association with prostatic utricle cysts and paraurethral glands in the female urethra {20060152; 22754140; 11812940; 23393356; 32960833}.

Data on the pathogenesis of clear cell adenocarcinoma are limited. Targeted exon sequencing of 4 clear cell adenocarcinomas demonstrated the presence of a pathogenic variant of PIK3CA in 3 cases; 2 of those 3 cases also had a KRAS pathogenic variant {31372739}. Next-generation sequencing analysis of one case showed novel gene fusion candidates including ANKRD28::FNDC3B, focal copy-number loss at the SMAD4 and ARID2 loci, and 38 somatic mutations including in the ATM and ALK genes {24389164}.
Clear cell adenocarcinoma forms a solitary polypoid or papillary, rarely ulcerative, mass with a mean size of 40 mm {11812940}.

The tumour displays papillary, tubulocystic, and/or solid growth patterns. The papillary fibrovascular cores may show hyalinization. Myxoid stromal reaction is common. The cells are flat, cuboidal, and hobnail, with clear, glycogen-rich, or eosinophilic cytoplasm. Cytological atypia is moderate to severe, with variable mitotic activity and necrosis. Tumours with relatively bland cytological features resembling nephrogenic adenoma have been described {20060152}. An associated urothelial carcinoma component or adjacent endometriotic foci may rarely be present {18381932}.

The cells are usually positive for CK7, CA125, PAX8, AMACR, HNF1β, p53, and napsin A. CK20 staining is variable {21496868; 18381932; 9865832}. They are negative for GATA3, p63, 34βE12, PSA, ER, PR, and WT1 {9865832; 32960833}.

PAX8 positivity and urothelial marker negativity differentiate clear cell adenocarcinoma from the clear cell (glycogen-rich) pattern of urothelial carcinoma. The histological and immunohistochemical overlap with nephrogenic adenoma can be difficult. Mitotic activity, invasive growth with involvement of the muscularis propria, hyperchromasia, and p53 staining are distinguishing features consistent with clear cell adenocarcinoma {9865832; 32960833; 20060152}.

Essential: a combination of solid, tubulocystic, and papillary growth patterns; hobnail cells with eosinophilic or clear cytoplasm.

Desirable: positivity for PAX8; negativity for urothelial markers.

Staging is based on the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) and Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) systems and is similar to that of urothelial tumours in the bladder and urethra. A histology-based urethral carcinoma staging system has been proposed for female urethral carcinomas, which provides better prognostic stratification than the AJCC system {32868524}.

Clear cell adenocarcinoma has been considered an aggressive tumour, with a 5-year survival rate of 40% for urethral or bladder clear cell adenocarcinoma {31555949; 31947882}. However, the clinical course is stage-driven, with patients presenting at an advanced stage more often than those with urothelial carcinoma. A stage-by-stage comparison of bladder tumours did not show significant differences between clear cell adenocarcinoma and urothelial carcinoma {31555949; 31947882; 32960833}. Advanced stage and poor prognosis are reported for clear cell adenocarcinomas in prostatic locations, whereas low-stage exophytic tumours are associated with good outcomes {32960833}.
